requirements.evidence: Three piece:full bases at q=-1,r=1, q=0,r=1, q=1,r=0 surrounding empty cell q=0,r=0 level 0. They form a triangle leaving the central hex empty, verified by get_build and top-down look.

requirements.requirement: Bay tray standing in that empty spot
requirements.evidence: bay:0#0,0#bay4 (hex-bin-bay-s-full-solid) placed at q=0,r=0 level 0 in the gap between the three bases, bolted to all three — offered as bay socket k=4 after the three bases were positioned.

finish.summary: Built three full hex bases in a triangle leaving cell 0,0,0 empty, then seated a full bay tray (hex-bin-bay-s-full-solid) in that central empty spot, capping open faces and locking joints. Mesh clash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three bases circling one gap — I'll seat your bay tray right in it.
